title: Byju's: NCLAT dismisses appeals by BCCI, Riju Raveendran against NCLT order on settlement
summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) in Chennai dismissed separate appeals by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and Riju Raveendran against an NCLT Bengaluru order. The NCLT had directed BCCI to withdraw its insolvency plea against Byju's and present a settlement proposal to the Committee of Creditors of the edtech group's parent company.
content:
The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) at Chennai on Thursday dismissed appeals by Riju Raveendran and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) challenging an NCLT Bengaluru order that directed BCCI to withdraw its insolvency plea against Byju's and place its settlement proposal before the Committee of Creditors (CoC) of the edtech entity's parent company.

The NCLAT ruling upholds the NCLT Bengaluru direction, leaving the question of the settlement proposal before the CoC intact. By dismissing the appeals, the appellate tribunal has effectively maintained the procedural route laid out by the NCLT for resolving the dispute between the parties.

The litigation involved both an external creditor body and an individual appellant, and centred on how an insolvency plea and any proposed settlement should be processed under the insolvency framework. The NCLT had earlier ruled that BCCI must withdraw its insolvency petition and present its settlement offer to the group’s creditors for consideration.

## Incident Details

The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) at Chennai on Thursday dismissed appeals by Riju Raveendran and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) challenging an NCLT Bengaluru order that directed BCCI to withdraw its insolvency plea against Byju's and place its settlement proposal before the Committee of Creditors (CoC) of the edtech entity's parent company.

## Ruling

The NCLAT ruling upholds the NCLT Bengaluru direction, leaving the question of the settlement proposal before the CoC intact. By dismissing the appeals, the appellate tribunal has effectively maintained the procedural route laid out by the NCLT for resolving the dispute between the parties.

## Background

The litigation involved both an external creditor body and an individual appellant, and centred on how an insolvency plea and any proposed settlement should be processed under the insolvency framework. The NCLT had earlier ruled that BCCI must withdraw its insolvency petition and present its settlement offer to the group’s creditors for consideration.

## Key points

- Appeals dismissed by NCLAT (Chennai): Riju Raveendran and BCCI
- NCLT Bengaluru order upheld: BCCI directed to withdraw insolvency plea
- Settlement proposal to be placed before the Committee of Creditors (CoC)
- Procedural route for resolving the dispute maintained
